questions.prompt: You opened the button, big blind called, flop A72 rainbow, you have AQ. Best default?

choices.text: Check back the nuts-adjacent hand with no plan

questions.explanation: Top pair top kicker on a dry single-raised board is a standard bet.

questions.prompt: You are the big blind caller on 9h 8h 7c with a pair and a draw. The button bets small. Best default?

choices.text: Continue. You have a real hand and equity.
Fold a pair and a draw to a small bet
All-in with no thought about the raise size

questions.explanation: Single-raised wet boards are where the caller’s range wakes up. Do not fold equity to a small bet.

questions.prompt: You opened, got called, and the flop is 876 two-tone. You have ace-high. Best default?

choices.text: Check back. This single-raised board favors the caller.
Bet because every open must c-bet

questions.explanation: Initiative is not a duty to bet every flop.

questions.prompt: Single-raised, out of position, you have a set and they bet. Best default?
questions.explanation: Sets in single-raised pots want a bigger pot while worse hands and draws exist.
